title: Does this gameplay montage feel AI-native, or just like regular browser game prototypes?
author: Fearless_Shift7108

comments.author: TsuinSensei
comments.body: That feels 100% AI and the expectation is that the games will never look and work like that.

comments.author: Lucaslouch
comments.body: definitely AI, not a single shot has logical physics

replies.author: Fearless_Shift7108
replies.body:
Yeah, that’s fair. The physics and logic are exactly the parts that need to be clearer. I think this montage made it look more like AI-generated footage than an actual playable system.

What we need to show next is real input, movement, and game rules working in-browser, not just visual variety. Appreciate the feedback — it helps point out what’s missing from the video.

comments.author: Lemonbicycle
comments.body: Sad that you need to ask.

comments.author: ArtArtArt123456
comments.body: Most people can tell something is ai through context clues. An overly high amount of detail is one such clue.

comments.author: Dry-Pickle-6121
comments.body: Yeah, the logic seems off. Like lines aren't lining up and other minute things. Overall the graphics are enticing but I can tell.

replies.author: Fearless_Shift7108
replies.body:
Thanks, that’s actually really helpful. I agree the graphics can look interesting, but if the logic feels off or the lines/movement don’t stay consistent, it still won’t feel like real gameplay.

This made me realize the next demo should focus less on montage shots and more on showing the actual playable loop: controls, rules, interactions, and how the game responds in real time.

comments.author: Low-Spell1867
comments.body: at no point does any of that look regular, its obviously AI especially when you see all the text artifacts and super off movements and graphics

comments.author: New_Acanthocephala62
comments.body: I mean.. the AI generated gameplay doesn't even make sense. And its obvious low quality AI because not a single clip had gameplay or visuals that made any sense.
